_comment: Course-level resource updates: point each course's hub links at its newest edition (2026 where it exists). Applied to Course.resources.lectures/assignments and description.

6.0001.description: Introduction to computer science and programming in Python, using MIT's newest OCW edition (6.100L, Fall 2022 video lectures by Ana Bell).

CS50X.description: CS50x 2026 — Harvard's introduction to the intellectual enterprises of computer science and the art of programming (David Malan).

CS61A.description: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs — the Fall 2026 edition of Berkeley's flagship programming course.

CS61B.description: UC Berkeley Data Structures — the live Fall 2026 edition (fa26.datastructur.es).

6.006.description: MIT Introduction to Algorithms — Spring 2020 OCW edition with full video lectures (Devadas, Demaine, Soloviev).

6.046J.description: MIT Design and Analysis of Algorithms — Spring 2015 OCW edition with full video lectures (Moshkovitz).

6.004.description: MIT Computation Structures (now 6.191) — OCW Spring 2017 edition with topic videos; live course at 6191.mit.edu.

6.828.description: MIT Operating System Engineering — the LIVE 6.1810 Fall 2026 xv6 course (successor of 6.828), Kaashoek & Morris.

6.829.description: MIT Computer Networks — OCW edition with complete lecture notes; topics ordered to the modern curriculum.

6.830.description: MIT Database Systems — the Redbook (free online) plus OCW Fall 2010 materials.

6.045J.description: Automata, Computability, and Complexity — MIT 18.404J Fall 2020 video edition (Sipser's course, recorded).

CSE341.description: Programming Languages (UW CSE341, Dan Grossman's curriculum) — studied through the PLAI book and interpreters you build.

6.036.description: MIT Introduction to Machine Learning — the interactive Open Learning Library edition (6.036 1T2019), with 6.036 Fall 2020 OCW notes.

CS188.description: UC Berkeley Introduction to Artificial Intelligence — Spring 2024 official lecture recordings (newest public edition).

6.858.description: MIT Computer Systems Security — Fall 2014 video edition (Zeldovich); the canonical recorded security course.

CS143.description: Stanford Compilers — the current course site; builds a complete Cool compiler (your Nand2Tetris compiler, professional scale).

CS142.description: Stanford Web Applications — the current course site; the full-stack payoff course of the path.
